# arXiv:2503.08964v1 [math.CO] 12 Mar 2025

List rainbow connection number of graphs

Rongxia Tang'

Henry Liuồi

Yueping Shit

12 March 2025

Chenming Wangt

Abstract

An edge-coloured path is rainbow if all of its edges have distinct colours. Let G

be a connected graph.

The rainbow connection number of G, denoted by rc(G), is the

minimum number of colours in an edge-colouring of G such that, any two vertices are connected by a rainbow path. The strong rainbow connection number of G, denoted by sre(G), is the minimum number of colours in an edge-colouring of G such that, any two vertices are connected by a rainbow geodesic (i.e., a path of shortest length). These two notions of connectivity of graphs were introduced by Chartrand, Johns, Mckeon and hang in 2008. In this paper, we introduce the list minbou connection number re (G). and the list strong rainbow connection number sre (G). These two parameters are the versions of re(G) and sre(G) that involve list edge-colourings. Among our results, we will determine the list rainbow connection number and list strong rainbow connection number of some specific graphs. We will also characterise all pairs of positive integers

a and & such that, there exists a connected graph G with src(G) = a and src (G) = b,

and similarly for the pair re' and sre.

. Finally, we propose the question of whether or

not we have re(G) = re (G), for all connected graphs G.

AMS Subject Classification (2020): 05C15

Keywords: List colouring: (strong) rainbow connection number

Introduction

In this paper, all graphs are finite, simple, and undirected. Let K, and C, denote the complete graph and cycle on n vertices. Let Kn.., denote the complete t-partite graph with class sizes ry,...ry. In particular, Km, is the complete bipartite graph with class sizes m and n. For 41,42,... ≥ 0, let Ki, ×1,4×2... denote the complete multipartite graph with t; classes of size i, for all i ≥ 1. Any subscript with t; = 0 is usually omitted. In particular, Kin denotes the complete t-partite graph where every class has size n. For a graph G
